synopsis: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D is described as a free, open material standard for environment creation and sensor simulation; version 1.0.0 was released on 3 April 2025 [f9178, f9181, f8360, f3714]. It addresses the insufficiency of geometry alone by letting one asset carry camera-, lidar- and radar-relevant material properties, including refractive index, roughness, permeability, wavelength-dependent lookup tables and per-material licence metadata [f4965, f12945, f3918, f13187]. Its usefulness for off-road objects remains tentative, and weather, lighting and sensor contamination are explicitly outside its scope, while volumetric properties remain under development [f7084, f13188, f9372, f3922]. Version 1.1.0 was planned for October 2026, with improved conductivity modelling and conversion of measured reflectance into BRDF, but the main page accessed that month still listed only 1.0.0 and the latest release found elsewhere was also 1.0.0 [f3923, f3924, f3925, f9182]. A vendor co-simulation demonstration combines OpenMATERIAL 3D with OpenSCENARIO, OSI and a physical lidar model, providing an implementation example rather than resolving the off-road applicability and scope gaps [f3981, f7084, f13188].
